name: Sea Turtle
description: Multi-decade magnetic homing using field inclination and intensity as biological GPS. Returns to natal beach after 30 years. Ocean current optimization provides 80% energy savings. Geomagnetic storm compensation adjusts navigation in real-time.

core_attributes.pattern: magnetic field navigation, generational homing, ocean current optimization

scope.definition: Accuracy of loggerhead sea turtle magnetic navigation — fraction of hatchlings swimming in magnetically appropriate direction when total darkness eliminates wave-following as cue, in rotating-coil experiments.

evidence.source: Lohmann & Lohmann (1994) 'Detection of magnetic inclination angle by sea turtles: a possible mechanism for determining latitude', Journal of Experimental Biology 190:69-78; Lohmann et al. (2001) 'Regional magnetic fields as navigational markers for sea turtles', Science 294:364-366.
cross_domain_examples: loggerhead hatchlings orient in geomagnetically appropriate direction in coil-manipulation experiments
magnetic map based on inclination + intensity allows position estimation without landmarks
salmon magnetic navigation at sea: convergent vertebrate geomagnetic positioning
migratory birds: magnetic compass using radical-pair mechanism in cryptochrome proteins — independent evolutionary origin

scope.falsifiability: If coil-manipulated sea turtles swim randomly when magnetic cues are the only available orientation cue, magnetic sensing is not operational in hatchlings.
scope.measurement_limits: Magnetic navigation provides coarse positional information (100-200 km accuracy). Chemical and visual cues provide fine-scale beach recognition. Solar and wave cues dominate in shallow coastal waters.

scope.definition: Return precision of adult female sea turtles to natal beach — distance from natal beach to nesting beach for adult females tracked by GPS, after 20-30 year oceanic migrations.

evidence.source: Bowen et al. (1993) 'Population structure of loggerhead turtles in the northwestern Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea', Conservation Biology 7:834-844; Luschi et al. (1998) natal homing tracking.
cross_domain_examples: green turtle females tracked to within 5 km of natal beach after 25-year absence
mitochondrial DNA clustering matches nesting beach locations — genetically encoded natal fidelity
Pacific salmon natal stream homing: analogous multi-year return precision to specific location

scope.falsifiability: If satellite-tracked adult females consistently nest on beaches >100 km from their natal beach (identified via genetic assignment), generational homing is not operating.
scope.measurement_limits: Homing accuracy is natal-beach size dependent — small beaches show higher precision than large continuous beaches. Genetic markers assign natal beach at 70-80 km resolution for most populations.

scope.definition: Energetic savings achieved by loggerhead sea turtle use of major ocean gyres during transoceanic developmental migration — ratio of actual swimming energy expenditure to direct-route equivalent.

evidence.source: Bolten (2003) 'Variation in sea turtle life history patterns', in 'The Biology of Sea Turtles vol 2'; Gaspar et al. (2006) loggerhead gyre-riding behavior.
cross_domain_examples: loggerhead hatchlings enter North Atlantic gyre system and ride current circuits requiring 30-40% less swimming energy than direct routes
albatross dynamic soaring uses wind gradients over ocean — analogous energy-free (or low-cost) long-distance travel
transoceanic sailing: human navigation optimizing ocean current use for energy-efficient passage (same principle)

scope.falsifiability: If satellite-tracked loggerheads show consistent cross-gyre swimming (against current) rather than gyre-following paths, current optimization is not the primary migration routing strategy.
scope.measurement_limits: Gyre utilization is species and age-class dependent. Adults return directly to nesting beaches, bypassing gyre circuits used by juveniles. Current optimization is a juvenile migration strategy.

scope.definition: Proportion of sea turtle navigational error introduced by moderate geomagnetic storms (Kp index 5-7) that is actively compensated vs persistent as navigational deviation over 48-hour tracking periods.

evidence.source: Lohmann et al. (2008) 'Geomagnetic imprinting: a unifying hypothesis of long-distance natal homing in salmon and sea turtles', PNAS 105:19096-19101.
cross_domain_examples: loggerhead turtles show increased swimming speed during geomagnetic storms — active reorientation behavior
homing pigeons lose 25-40% navigation accuracy during solar maximum geomagnetic disturbances
submarine navigation using inertial reference: analogous drift compensation strategy during GPS blackout

scope.falsifiability: If tracking shows turtle paths deviate proportionally to storm intensity with no recovery over 48h, turtles cannot compensate for geomagnetic storm noise.
scope.measurement_limits: Compensation evidence is indirect — behavioral speed change is a proxy for active reorientation. Direct evidence requires concurrent magnetometry and tracking data across multiple storms.
